acquisitions.title: AWS Weekly Roundup: Welcome DuckLabs to the team, Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), and more (August 31, 2026)
acquisitions.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has signed a definitive agreement to acquire DuckLabs, which is the Amsterdam-based company behind the open-source analytical database DuckDB. DuckDB will remain open source under an independent foundation and the MIT licence while being led by its co-founders, Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt. The database operates locally or on Amazon S3 and is designed to execute SQL directly against files such as Parquet, CSV, and JSON. AWS plans to integrate DuckDB's query speed with enterprise-scale services including Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, and Amazon Athena over time. The technology is also intended to be combined with analytics tools like Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon SageMaker. DuckDB is noted for handling everyday queries of a terabyte or less and pairs effectively with artificial intelligence agents. Vice President and Distinguished Engineer Andy Warfield discussed the acquisition and analytics trends in a post on the All Things Distributed blog. The announcement was part of the weekly roundup published on the official AWS News Blog.

launches.title: Accelerating the borderless Lakehouse: Announcing preview of cross-cloud caching
launches.excerpt: Google Cloud has announced the preview of cross-cloud caching and cross-cloud connections for its borderless Lakehouse platform. These new features aim to reduce the costs and network transfer volumes associated with querying distributed enterprise data estates. Modern organisations frequently store information across multiple locations, including Amazon S3, Azure Data Lake Storage, and various SaaS platforms. Historically, uniting these distributed datasets required complex ETL pipelines and expensive data transfers. The borderless Lakehouse addresses this by allowing organisations to query data in place using the Apache Iceberg REST catalog specification. The newly introduced cross-cloud caching feature transparently accelerates queries in BigQuery by storing frequently accessed data locally in Google Cloud. Operating at a sub-file block granularity, the cache retains specific column chunks rather than entire multi-gigabyte files. Cached data blocks are protected using default encryption at rest via Google-managed encryption keys. Furthermore, cache entries remain strictly partitioned by project and regional boundaries to support compliance requirements. Alongside caching, the preview of BigQuery cross-cloud connections enables users to query non-Iceberg data stored in other cloud environments.

launches.title: The new AgentCore Runtime is now available in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
launches.excerpt: Amazon Web Services has announced the availability of the next generation of AgentCore Runtime, which is the serverless microVM compute within Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The updated runtime provides elastic memory management that reclaims unused memory during a session so that users pay for actual usage instead of peak consumption. It also offers consistent cold start times regardless of container image size or concurrency levels. The service retains the existing serverless model features, including no pre-provisioning, scaling to zero, hardware-enforced session isolation, and pay-per-use pricing. Under the new memory management approach, each session begins with a small memory profile, and additional memory is allocated on demand as workloads require it. For cold starts, the runtime prepares the agent environment once and creates a snapshot, allowing new instances to restore from that snapshot instead of repeating the full startup sequence. During testing, the new runtime achieved a P75 cold start time of 1.9 to 2.0 seconds for container images ranging from 200 megabytes to 2 gigabytes, compared to 5.4 to 30 seconds for version one. The upgraded runtime is currently available in five specific regions, namely us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1, and ap-northeast-1. Users can begin utilising the new runtime by setting the platformVersion parameter to V2 when they create or update a runtime environment.

launches.title: New low-cost burstable Amazon EC2 T8i instances are generally available
launches.excerpt: Amazon has announced the general availability of new low-cost burstable EC2 T8i instances powered by custom sixth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable Processors. These instances deliver up to thirty percent better price performance compared to previous generation T3 instances and are designed for low-to-moderate CPU utilization workloads. Target applications include microservices, low-traffic websites, development and testing environments, data processing jobs, and login gateways. The new instances continue to use the burstable performance model, providing a baseline level of CPU performance with the ability to exceed that baseline using CPU credits. Unlimited mode is set as the default credit configuration on T8i instances, which offer four sizes ranging from nano to medium. They maintain unique vCPU-to-memory ratios of one to zero point two five, one to zero point five, and one to one. Customers can purchase these instances as On-Demand or Spot instances, while the micro and small sizes are also included in the AWS Free Tier. T8i instances support shared tenancy exclusively and do not accommodate Dedicated tenancy or Dedicated Hosts. They are available immediately across multiple AWS regions in North America, Asia-Pacific, Canada, and Europe, with Savings Plan options expected in the future.

geo.title: Trump says his planned triumphal arch will double as a military complex to store ammunition
geo.excerpt: US President Donald Trump has announced that his proposed triumphal arch project will now double as a military complex capable of storing equipment, ammunition, and deploying snipers and drones. Writing on his Truth Social platform, Trump stated that the plans were being updated at the strong request of the US military for national security purposes. He explained that the facility will house large quantities of sniper ammunition and provide the rapid ability to use drones and snipers from the roof and plaza areas. Trump did not disclose specific construction timelines or details regarding whether the updated facility requires further approval. He noted that Washington DC is apparently the only capital among fifty-nine top global cities that currently lacks a triumphal arch. Construction on the 250-foot monument, planned for a site across the Potomac River from Washington DC near Arlington National Cemetery, was expected to begin this month. Earlier design renderings feature a golden, winged Lady Liberty flanked by gold eagles, alongside gold inscriptions of patriotic phrases. Standing at 76 metres, the structure will surpass the nearby Lincoln Memorial in height while reaching half the elevation of the Washington Monument. The BBC has contacted the Department of Defence to request further information about the revised plans. The arch represents one of several major construction and remodelling initiatives pursued by Trump during his second term to alter the appearance of the US capital.

invest.title: ‘It's awful’: How tariffs, soaring fuel costs and higher interest rates are squeezing American companies
invest.excerpt: American businesses are facing a challenging economic environment driven by a combination of tariffs, surging fuel prices, and rising interest rates. Companies across manufacturing, transportation, and retail are experiencing a three-way squeeze that increases the cost of raw materials, production, and financing. Middle-market manufacturers and capital-intensive sectors are particularly affected because they must contend with record diesel prices and expensive short-term lending. While large technology and finance firms with substantial cash reserves remain largely insulated, smaller suppliers and automotive companies are seeing their profit margins shrink significantly. For example, some domestic auto parts makers have cancelled expansion plans or halted manufacturing operations entirely due to rising material costs. Conversely, major airlines have successfully passed increased fuel expenses onto travelers by raising fares and reducing less profitable flight routes. Executives across multiple industries note that widespread price increases have become unavoidable as organizations struggle to absorb mounting operational expenses. Although corporate profit margins generally remain near historic highs, economists warn that aggressive interest rate hikes could slow the broader economy without directly resolving underlying supply chain and energy pressures.

invest.title: Top Wall Street analysts find these 3 stocks attractive as long-term investments
invest.excerpt: Investors navigating market volatility can look to recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to identify companies with strong long-term growth potential. According to TipRanks performance data, three specific stocks are currently favoured by leading market professionals. Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci has reiterated a buy rating on enterprise software and cloud infrastructure firm Oracle with a price target of $400. DiFucci highlights Oracle as a long-term investment driven by opportunities in artificial intelligence training and inferencing, alongside its traditional public cloud business. Furthermore, Oracle reported better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027, bolstered by solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue. Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale has initiated coverage on space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab with a buy rating and an $80 price target. Gesuale points to the company's pending Iridium acquisition, which will establish Rocket Lab as a vertically integrated space company with positive free cash flow and a substantial backlog. In addition, J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth has upgraded Meta Platforms to a buy rating and increased his price target to $820. Anmuth notes that Meta is positioned for significant upside due to the early-stage rollout of its frontier models, AI-powered offerings, and expanding infrastructure capacity across its extensive user base.

invest.title: Williams-Sonoma's stock has soared in a sluggish housing market. Here's how it won over Wall Street
invest.excerpt: Williams-Sonoma has emerged as one of the top-performing retail stocks of the year, with its share price climbing about 23% by late September and over 200% across a three-year period. This outperformance has occurred amidst a sluggish American housing market driven by high interest rates, which typically depresses home goods sales. Chief Executive Laura Alber attributed the company's success to improvements in product quality, service, and storytelling that attract new shoppers. Key to this resilience has been the enhancement of underlying business fundamentals, including a significant expansion in operating margins during challenging post-pandemic years. The retailer achieved this largely by reducing promotions, selling products at full price, and optimising its supply chain for home deliveries. Furthermore, e-commerce accounts for more than two-thirds of the company's sales, bolstered by the introduction of an artificial intelligence sales assistant and supply chain applications. Business-to-business sales have also grown significantly, while its largest brand, Pottery Barn, has experienced renewed same-store sales growth. Despite these positive results, the business faces potential risks from tariffs because over 80% of its merchandise purchases in 2025 originated from foreign manufacturers. Nevertheless, the firm previously received a substantial tariff refund following a Supreme Court ruling, distributing portions of the funds to employees and vendors while keeping the money separate from reported earnings. Analysts note that the company's multi-brand portfolio and omnichannel approach provide a strong competitive advantage in the fragmented furniture industry.

invest.title: Caruso-Cabrera: The investing tailwinds for Latin America are the best in decades
invest.excerpt: Latin American equities are currently outperforming the S&P 500, with the iShares Latin America 40 ETF rising fifteen percent year to date and more than seventy percent since late 2024. A recent report from Citi indicates that regional growth conditions are the strongest in decades, driven by a weak United States dollar, strong commodity prices, and favorable geopolitics. Additional support comes from modern central banking practices that have successfully controlled inflation, alongside some of the highest real interest rates globally. Furthermore, recent elections have brought pro-business leaders to power, encouraging foreign exchange inflows and strengthening diplomatic ties with the United States. Country-specific catalysts include Mexico benefiting from technology exports and Argentina experiencing a market-friendly economic shift. Private capital flows have consequently been reenergized, with European investors committing more funds to Latin American stocks in 2026 than at any point in the prior sixteen years. Despite these positive indicators, the region faces potential risks, most notably the threat of rising United States interest rates and weather disruptions caused by El Nino affecting the agricultural sector. Citigroup analysts note that while market valuations already reflect some of these opportunities, improved corporate earnings could drive further global capital reallocation. Meanwhile, the expansion of digital banking services is creating new financial opportunities across the region. Additionally, upcoming presidential elections in Brazil present a significant near-term catalyst following polls showing a tight race for the presidency.
